messages.author: 4c1108aaddb5744d
messages.subject: Problems in plotting yearly data
parts:
Hi all,

I have some problems in plotting time series data. For example, I have several datasets, df1, df2, df3, etc., while each dataset has the same structure. Different datasets represent flow at different gauges.

df1
year   month   day   flow    time
2002    1           1       5      2002-01-01
2002    1           2       6      2002-01-02
2002    1           3       5.5   2002-01-03
...

df2
year   month   day   flow    time
2002    1           1      7.5    2002-01-01
2002    1           2      8       2002-01-02
2002    1           3      7.6    2002-01-03
...

I tried to plot daily time-series data, using the code:
p1 = ggplot()+ geom_line(data=df1,aes(x=time,y=flow,color='DF1') + geom_line(data=df2,aes(x=time,y=flow,color='DF2') + scale_color_manual('',limits=c('DF1', 'DF2'), values=c('red', 'blue'))
print(p1)

Now I want to plot annual values, but got no luck. Could anyone tell me the problem? Thanks.
df1.yr = aggregate(flow~year, data=df1, sum)
df2.yr = aggregate(flow~year, data=df2, sum)
...

p2 = ggplot()+ geom_line(data=df1.yr, aes(x=year,y=flow, color='DF1.yr')+ geom_line(data=df2.yr, aes(x=year,y=flow,color='DF2.yr')+ scale_color_manual('', limits=c('DF2.yr', 'DF2.yr'), values=c('red','blue'))
print(p2)

It has the error message:
Don't know how to automatically pick scale for object of type function. Defaulting to continuous.
Error in data.frame(x =, y= function (save = 'default', status=0, :arguments imply differing number of rows:

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Problems in plotting yearly data
parts:
I think you need to combine your datasets into one and then plot. 

see:
dplyr::bind_rows()

I would also suggest a mutate step to add a new column that defines the dataset that you can then color by later. 

df1 %>%
mutate(colorby = "DF1")
df2 %>%
mutate(colorby = "DF2")

If you have a lot of datasets, you might want to look into some other method that is more generic for creating a column that is the name of the dataframe/tibble. 

B
